text:
maria: Quick proposal — we should try a "precision concierge" pattern: per-customer progressive canaries that start traffic on FP8, then INT8, then 4-bit if quality holds. idea is to keep a fast lane for heavy customers but gate degradation per-customer rather than globally.

devon: sounds promising. how do you want to measure "quality holds"? do we rely on existing degscore latency or do a separate eval set per customer?

maria: separate eval sets per customer where possible (critical customers), fallback to a small shadow prompt-set for everyone else. acceptance signal = combined BLEU-ish + regression on a few golden prompts + prompt-response embedding drift under 0.05. also check hallucination indicator.

alex: curious about rollout speed. what % traffic do you anneal at and what's the hysteresis?

maria: start 1% for 24h with shadow logging, if metrics stable -> 5% for 6h -> 25% for 12h -> 100% (or stop at any fail). hysteresis: if any metric regresses by >2x threshold we immediately cut to previous stage; if KV cache hit rate drops >5% revert too.

sam: operationally, how do we wire this into the runtime? will each request include a precision override header or will routing be based on customer id?

alex: prefer routing by customer id at the smart-router layer. keep runtime decision minimal: server sees model variant and whether KV cache matches. we avoid per-request heavyweight negotiation.

maria: agreed. plan: orchestrator sets a "concierge_profile" for each customer in route table. runtime gets precomputed variant and quant profile. fallbacks configured as a list.

devon: can we see a sample profile format?

alex: here's a minimal sketch to prototype (ops, ignore indentation if I botched):

```yaml
concierge_profile:
  customer: acme-inc
  stages:
    - name: fp8-canary
      percent: 1
      duration_hours: 24
      metrics:
        - name: embedding-drift
          threshold: 0.05
        - name: golden-regression
          threshold: 0.02
    - name: int8-warmup
      percent: 5
      duration_hours: 6
    - name: int8-broad
      percent: 25
      duration_hours: 12
    - name: int4-roll
      percent: 100
  fallbacks:
    - name: fp32
      reason: quality-fail
```

sam: nice. question: telemetry cost. per-customer shadow evals and embeddings cost tokens. do we budget that from customer's quota or platform?

maria: platform should absorb a small fixed overhead for stability; optional opt-in where customer pays for larger bespoke evals. we'll surface expected extra token cost in console.

devon: failure modes? any risk of correlated degradation across customers (e.g., model patch makes FP8 worse globally)?

maria: good point — we still run global model-level smoke checks before promoting any quant variant cluster-wide. concierge is an additional safety layer, not the only gate.

alex: ops-bot just posted a small incident simulation script. runs locally and emits a pass/fail. can we attach it to canary automation?

ops-bot: automation: simulated-canary-run for acme-inc started. logs: 200 sims, 1 failure (response drift 0.06) -> status: FAIL.

sam: thanks, ops-bot. that simulation suggests our thresholds are tight but workable. if a single sim fails we should avoid fully failing on a noisy outlier; maybe require sustained delta over a window.

maria: agreed — change policy: require failure rate >1% across sims or sustained delta (3 consecutive windows) before rollback. will update RFC.

devon: one more thing — how does this interact with caching? KV cache differences between FP8 and int8 could hurt long-context apps. do we version caches per-precision?

alex: yes, we must namespace KV cache by quant-profile id. otherwise sequence mismatches will cause subtle state corruption. also need a migration step for pinned sessions.

maria: we'll add cache-namespace and a session flag for "precision-bound". sessions pinned to a precision can't be auto-migrated. that will be a customer-visible constraint.

sam: doc/console change needed: show pinned sessions and estimated tail-latency delta.

maria: I'll open a doc PR and a console ticket. next steps: prototype orchestration changes, add profile schema tests, run sims for top 10 customers. thanks all. :rocket:
